candidates.rationale: The reproduced lost updates among cooperating sessions are fixed by one persistent base-directory flock held over all reads and writes. Each invocation opens a fresh lock descriptor; thread-local context validates ownership without sharing a flock open-file description between concurrent calls. Independent cross-project barriers and same-instance threads preserve changes; reviewed shared tests also observe a child blocked on the native flock and successful continuation after a fixture child exits. This is local POSIX cooperation, not a transaction or protection against writers ignoring the protocol. A supplemental warmup plus eight concurrent calls on four threads, two projects and eight distinct instances retained all nine session IDs and all project changes/decisions after reopening; the latest ghost for each project matched its latest system session.

limits: Atomic visibility is per JSON file. Project, ghosts and system have three possible commit points; a failed consolidation can leave one or two confirmed files plus a current visible-but-unsynced or unknown replacement. No automatic global rollback/recovery protocol is added.

flock serializes cooperating local POSIX callers of crystallize_session. Direct private _write_json calls are atomic file replacements only; noncooperating writers, hostile directory/lock substitution, cross-host/network filesystems and multi-file reader snapshots are not isolated.
Identity/metadata checks narrow ordinary races but are not atomic with replace/unlink. No confinement claim against an actor modifying paths between the final check and mutation.

File and directory fsync order is tested. Filesystem/storage guarantees, power loss and hardware durability were not tested. REPLACED records observed visibility, not confirmed durability after a failed sync.

Abrupt owned child exits are process tests, not power-cut simulations. A partial temporary can remain orphaned; it is deliberately not purged by name/age. The persistent lock inode remains and is never deleted for recovery.
The existing JSON schema and intentional history limits are retained; this is not full nested-schema validation or a migration. New timestamps use UTC; historical values are not reinterpreted.
Mode permission bits are copied; broad metadata/ACL/xattr preservation is not claimed or tested.

No real HOME/.agent/memory, operator data, external service, protected runtime or hardware was used. Parent aggregate-suite, MyPy and documentation results are not substituted for the reviewer commands recorded here.
